title: var Hoisting Trap

bugs.explanation: `var` declarations are hoisted to the top of the function but not their assignments, so `console.log(x)` on line 2 prints `undefined` instead of throwing a ReferenceError as the developer likely expects. Use `let` or `const` on line 3 instead — they are not hoisted in the same way and would produce a ReferenceError, making the bug visible at runtime.

title: Loose Equality Instead of Strict

bugs.explanation: Using `==` performs type coercion, so `0 == false` evaluates to `true`. This means empty strings and `null` would also pass. Use `===` for strict equality: `value === 0` to check specifically for zero.

title: typeof null Returns 'object'

bugs.explanation: `typeof null` returns `'object'` due to a historical JavaScript bug, so `isObject(null)` returns `true` even though `null` is not an object. Add a null check: `if (val !== null && typeof val === 'object')`.

title: Arrow Function Missing Return

bugs.explanation: When an arrow function uses curly braces `{}`, it requires an explicit `return` statement. Without it, the function returns `undefined`. Fix: `return n * 2;`, or use the implicit return form: `const double = (n) => n * 2;`.

title: const Object Mutation Is Allowed (No Bugs)
Array push Returns Length, Not Array

bugs.explanation: `Array.push()` returns the new length of the array (3), not the modified array. `updated` will be `3`, not `['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']`. To get the updated array, push separately and reference `fruits` directly.

title: parseInt Without Radix

bugs.explanation: `parseInt` without a radix argument can misinterpret strings — in older environments, strings starting with `0` were parsed as octal, making `'08'` and `'09'` return `0`. Always pass the radix explicitly: `parseInt(v, 10)`.

title: Using the Return Value of forEach

bugs.explanation: `forEach` always returns `undefined` — it does not build a new array. `doubled` will be `undefined`. Use `map` instead: `const doubled = numbers.map(n => n * 2);`.

title: Closure in Loop With var

bugs.explanation: `var` is function-scoped, not block-scoped. By the time the `setTimeout` callbacks fire, the loop has finished and `i` is `3`, so all three callbacks print `3` instead of `0`, `1`, `2`. Replace `var` with `let` — `let` is block-scoped, so each iteration captures its own copy of `i`.

title: Falsy Check Catches Valid Zero

bugs.explanation: `0 == false` is `true` because `==` coerces both sides to numbers. A valid score of `0` incorrectly prints `'No score recorded'`. Use strict equality and check explicitly: `if (score === null || score === undefined)`.

title: Off-By-One With <=

bugs.explanation: Array indices run from `0` to `length - 1`. Using `<=` causes one extra iteration where `i === items.length`, accessing `items[3]` which is `undefined`. Change `i <= items.length` to `i < items.length`.

title: NaN Comparison With !==

bugs.explanation: `NaN` is the only JavaScript value not equal to itself — `NaN !== NaN` is always `true`, so this condition is always true regardless of `n`. Use `Number.isNaN(n)` to correctly detect NaN: `if (!Number.isNaN(n))`.

title: Missing break in switch

bugs.explanation: The `case 'Monday'` block is missing a `break` statement. Without it, execution falls through to `case 'Friday'` and also prints `'End of work week'`. Add `break;` after line 4.

title: this Lost in Callback

bugs.explanation: Inside a regular function callback, `this` is not the `timer` object — it refers to the global object (or `undefined` in strict mode). `this.seconds` won't update `timer.seconds`. Use an arrow function instead: `setInterval(() => { ... }, 1000)` so `this` is inherited from the enclosing `start` method.

title: Missing await in Async Function

bugs.explanation: Both `fetch()` and `.json()` return Promises. Without `await`, `response` is a Promise object (not the HTTP response), and calling `.json()` on a Promise throws a TypeError. Add `await` to both: `const response = await fetch(...)` and `const data = await response.json()`.

title: undefined + 1 Produces NaN

bugs.explanation: `config.timeout` is `undefined` because the property doesn't exist on the empty object. `undefined + 1` produces `NaN`. Add a fallback: `const newValue = (config.timeout ?? 0) + 1;`.

title: Wrong Ternary Precedence

bugs.explanation: `+` binds tighter than `:`, so this parses as `age >= 18 ? 'adult' : ('minor' + ' (needs guardian)')`. If the intent was to append `' (needs guardian)'` to both branches, use explicit parentheses: `(age >= 18 ? 'adult' : 'minor') + ' (needs guardian)'`.

title: Clean String Truncate (No Bugs)
Clean Array Deduplication (No Bugs)
Filter With == true Misses Non-1 Values

bugs.explanation: `s == true` coerces `true` to `1`, so only elements that equal `1` after coercion pass. `10`, `42`, and `7` are all excluded because `10 == true` is `false`. The correct filter to remove zeros is `s => s !== 0` or simply `scores.filter(Boolean)`.
